days.label: Monday
days.text: Monday gets going at Fletcher Free Library, where the weekly Shakespeare Out Loud group finishes reading Romeo and Juliet from 4 to 5:30, no experience needed and listeners welcome. At 6, UVM professor Ken Allen talks through the causes of Vermont's healthcare crisis and his case for single payer at the Burlington Friends Meeting House on North Prospect Street. Bird people can head to Phoenix Books on Church Street at 7, where Oregon author Marina Richie launches Feathered Forest in conversation with Vermont birder Trish O'Kane, free with an RSVP. Ora Cogan with Alice Grace over at Foam Brewers with doors at 7 and haunted folk and shadowy country at 7:30. Higher Ground splits the night between rapper Chandler , of the viral hit FIGURE IT OUT, in the Showcase Lounge at 7:30 and Cate Le Bon ($36) in the Ballroom at 8 with her seventh record, Michelangelo Dying. Empyrean fans have a late one, as Phoenix Books in Essex Junction throws a free midnight release party for Threshing Day , Rebecca Yarros's new book, from 10 until midnight with trivia, bookmark making and quadrant attire encouraged.

days.label: Tuesday
days.text: Tuesday opens big at UVM, where the free all day Vermont Summit on energy, health and the economy fills the Davis Center starting at 9, with a 10 AM keynote from Nate Hagens of The Great Simplification podcast, registration required. From noon to 3:30 the Champlain Valley Expo hosts a free Community Career & Job Fair built around hands on stations like a heavy equipment simulator, VR welding, a snowplow and a mini F-16, with on the spot applications through the Department of Labor. At 5, former Agriculture Secretary Roger Allbee gives the Samuel Hand Lecture at UVM's Billings Library on 250 years of Vermont farming, with hearty refreshments after, and Spoonful Herbals leads Autumn Bitter Root Remedies at Shelburne Farms, a weed walk that ends with bitter roots turned into fall tonics. Cyclists get a one time sunset edition of Local Motion's monthly EZ Breezy ride , leaving 1 Steele Street at 6 for a flat 20 mile out and back on the Causeway, join for any part and bring lights for the ride home. Also at 6, Protect Our Winters brings Stoke Fest to Main Street Landing with outdoor and climate films, a conversation hosted by pro skier Brody Leven and free Ben & Jerry's, UVM men's soccer hosts UMass at Virtue Field, and Karma Bird House hosts drop in figure drawing from 6 to 8, with the last Tuesday of every month set aside for long poses. In Shelburne, local author Áille Róis talks about her novel Twisted Obsession and indie publishing at Pierson Library at 6:30, and at 7:30 Destroyer with Ryley Walker plays the Higher Ground Showcase Lounge.

days.label: Wednesday
days.text: Wednesday means our own Pick-up Basketball [MEETUP] at Pomeroy Park at 5:30, outdoors and free, so come get some runs in. Earlier in the day, Winooski celebrates the end of three years of construction with the Main Street ribbon cutting at the VFW on Maple Street at 10, free and open to all, to show off wider sidewalks, a northbound bike lane and 132 new trees. Vermont Master Naturalist Gene O. Desideraggio leads a tree ID and natural history tour of Oakledge Park from noon to 2, and ticket sales close today at 2. The Meatpackers play the donut porch at Shelburne Orchards from 12:30 to 1:30, their mix of bluegrass, gospel and redneck. The Queer Horror Book Club meets at the Hunny Hive on Church Street at 5:30 to talk Exquisite Corpse by Poppy Z. Brite, and on the waterfront SAVU pairs yin yoga, chanting and sound healing with an hour of sauna and cold plunge in Yin & Sacred Sound with Kishori ($50) . Runners can join a 5K loop run [MEETUP] from outside the Black Flannel taproom in Essex Junction at 5:30 with social time after, and the library's Vegan in Vermont cookbook club holds a potluck at 6 with the owner of Fresh & Foraged talking about safely gathering wild plants and mushrooms, registration required. May Day on North Winooski Avenue hosts Piedmont winemaker Crotin 1897 for one night only, so grab a dinner reservation. At 7:30 the big shows split up, with Grammy winning jazz singer Samara Joy and her septet at the Flynn and Anberlin , whose Vega is their first album in ten years, in the Higher Ground Ballroom.

days.label: Thursday
days.text: Thursday is October 1 and the warmest day of the stretch. Mayor Emma Mulvaney-Stanak holds her North District Mayor Meetup at the Bagel Café on North Avenue from 8 to 9 AM, and the Essex Art League welcomes guests at 9 at the First Congregational Church of Essex Junction, where illustrator Ginny Joyner shares stories from more than 25 years of freelance work and leads an activity, so bring a black pen and a sketchbook. At 1, local artist Julia Davenport teaches a free Zentangle workshop at Burnham Memorial Library in Colchester with all materials provided, and from 4:30 to 6:30 Outdoor Gear Exchange lets you try Teva's new Trailpeak trail runners on Catamount's trails in Williston, with snacks and a chance to win a pair. South Burlington's Park Hop Brews beer garden lands at Szymanski Park from 5:30 to 7:30 with DJ Dakota, Pizza 44 and glow in the dark pickleball. At 7, Queen City Ghostwalk creator Thea Lewis launches True Crime Stories of Vermont at Phoenix Books on Church Street, free with an RSVP, Merit Kahn opens her one woman comedy show Optimistic Personality Disorder at Off Center, the Forever 38 crew heads to trivia at Burlington Beer Company [MEETUP] , and violinist Claire Wells and pianist Pualina Lim play Debussy, Prokofiev, Brahms and Bartók at An Evening of Masterworks in Vermont Public's Stetson Studio in Colchester. The Burlington Odd Fellows host weekly drop in figure drawing at their North Avenue hall from 7 to 9, by suggested donation. Southern Culture on the Skids brings its wobbly Americana to the Higher Ground Showcase Lounge at 7:30, Standing Stone Wines in Winooski does Witch, Crafts & Halloween at 8 with music from Daniel Ouellette and then Elvira on the screen while everyone crafts, and Karaoke in the Alley gets going in the alley at Red Square at 8.
